# Psalms of Solomon — Psalm 1 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Vindobonensis) | **Section:** Lament over Jerusalem's Defilement

---

**1:1** I cried out to the LORD in my great distress,
unto God when the sinners assailed.

**1:2** Suddenly the clamor of war was heard before me;
"He will hear me, for I am full of righteousness."

**1:3** I thought in my heart that I was full of righteousness,
for I had prospered and had many children.

**1:4** Their wealth spread to the whole earth,
and their glory unto the end of the earth.

**1:5** They were exalted unto the stars;
they said they would never fall.

**1:6** They were insolent in their prosperity,
and they had no understanding.

**1:7** Their sins were in secret,
and even I had no knowledge of them.

**1:8** Their lawless deeds surpassed the gentiles before them;
they utterly profaned the sanctuary of the LORD.

---

*EMET notes: Translated from the Greek (Codex Vindobonensis). Hyphenated compounds preserve construct chains. Bracketed words [thus] are implied by grammar but absent from the surface text. The psalm opens in first-person lament before transitioning to third-person accusation of Jerusalem's sinners.*
